note: Rustic DNR state-forest campground at the Huntersville canoe landing on the Crow Wing River, a put-in and take-out for paddlers, between Nimrod and Menahga. Wooded sites in a north loop and spurs south of the landing. More than 150 miles of forest roads and logging trails for hiking, shared with vehicles. Managed by Itasca State Park. Distinct from the separate Shell City horse camp in this forest. --Claude
summary: DNR facility cmp00028 read: 24 primitive sites (1 accessible), 5 vault toilets, 2 wells, $17 tax-included paid online same day (stored 'fee on site' corrected). Crow Wing River measured ~26 m wide at the campground: riverfront -> creekside proposed. Phone 218-266-2100 -> 218-699-7251 (Itasca SP, DNR manager). Website hyphen.
flags: WATERFRONT riverfront -> creekside proposed (by size): the Crow Wing River measures about 25-27 m of open water at the campground on Esri z19 (46.7390,-94.9283: west bank to east bank ~26 m; at 46.7395,-94.9286 ~26.6 m), under the ~30 m riverfront threshold. Sites are not numbered on any DNR page (facility map cmp00028.pdf returns 404). The north-loop spur ends (about 46.7395,-94.9286) and the landing clearing (about 46.7384,-94.9285) lie roughly 10-35 m from the water; on leaf-off imagery the ground between is open under scattered pines and bare hardwoods, but leaf-on NAIP shows near-continuous canopy along the bank. Reviewer may take it further down to not waterfront on the canopy rule; creekside is the most it can hold.
FEES note corrected: stored note said 'first come, first served, paid at the campground' and the entry note 'Fee on site'; the DNR fee page says 'DNR does not accept self-payment envelopes on site'.
PHONE 218-266-2100 -> 218-699-7251: the DNR facility record names Itasca State Park (218-699-7251) as manager; Google Maps lists the same number.

Pin 46.73830,-94.92900 matches the DNR facility point 46.738306,-94.929115; no move. No DNR alerts; season not stated by the DNR. The DNR description calls the river the 'Crow River'; it is the Crow Wing River (DNR water trail; the Crow River is a different river far south).
